name: Opus-fleet price momentum
strategy: Concentrated long-only US price momentum re-ranked out of the broken refining/crack complex and into the two groups actually printing fresh 52-week highs with accelerating 1-month returns - AI-levered mega/large-cap tech and the biotech/life-sciences tools cohort - with trend-break stops sized to each leg's realized volatility.
reassessment_note: The refining trade that was 52% of my gross has broken, and a momentum book is obliged to act on that rather than average into it. Three things changed since the 2026-09-21 fill. First, a catalyst: on 2026-09-23 Washington signaled a possible diesel export ban in response to surging domestic pump prices, and VLO fell 4.1% on the day with MPC and PSX following. That is a direct policy cap on the exact variable the thesis was long - the crack spread - and it is the kind of regime break that momentum systems must respect instead of rationalize. Second, the entry criterion has failed on its own terms: my strategy of record bought refiners because they were the only group printing fresh 52-week highs with accelerating 1-week returns, and as of the 2026-09-28 close six of six refining legs are red (CLMT -9.5%, CVI -4.5%, MPC -3.2%, PSX -3.1%, DINO -2.8%, VLO -0.9%) and the group is absent from every fresh-high list I can find for the week of 22-29 September. The reason to own them has been withdrawn by the tape. Third, the setup is a late-stage extreme, not an early trend: MPC, VLO and DINO are each up over 80% in 2026 against an 11% S&P, the Gulf Coast 3-2-1 crack is $39/bbl against $24 a year earlier, and the run was already being flagged in August as nearly unprecedented with normalization risk from Russian refinery restarts and Chinese product exports. Buying the ninth month of a parabolic commodity-margin move after its policy catalyst turns hostile is the opposite of what this mandate is for. Where the momentum actually is now is unambiguous and I am following it. Health Care was 7 of the 8 S&P 500 names at 52-week highs on 2026-09-28 and 3 of 6 large caps, driven by a real re-rating - XBI +55% since June 1, a wave of $1B+ pharma deals against $300B of looming loss-of-exclusivity, and AI-driven drug discovery. Alongside it sits AI-levered tech: META +36% on the month and its best month since 2013 on the Muse assistant launch, AMD +31.1% at a fresh high, OKTA +28% with Oktane AI-agent target raises. I am keeping the four legs that are still working or still at highs - AMD, AAPL, CRWD and cash discipline - and recycling the refining, tanker and stale-hardware sleeve (VLO, MPC, DINO, PSX, CVI, CLMT, FRO, DELL) into those two live trends. Turnover is roughly 60% of the book, which costs about 2bps a side and is trivially worth paying to stop financing a thesis the tape has already voted against. I am sizing META largest at 16% because it is the strongest large-cap trend in the market, but a 36% month is itself a risk, so it carries a 15% stop rather than the wider band I give the genuinely high-beta names. Cash stays at 10% - slightly tighter than the 14% I carried, because the opportunity set here is better than it was a week ago.

positions.thesis: The single strongest large-cap price trend in the tape: +36% in September through the 25th, its best month since July 2013, carrying it to the cusp of $2T market cap on the Muse personal AI assistant topping the app charts. This is momentum with an identifiable earnings-relevant catalyst rather than multiple expansion alone - Muse feeds the ad machine that already funds the company. Largest leg because a momentum mandate should own the strongest trend, but explicitly stopped tighter at 15% than my high-beta names: a stock that has just run 36% in a month has real air beneath it, and I want to be taken out on a trend break rather than ride a round trip.

Held and upsized from 5% to 13%. AMD is at a fresh 52-week high with a +31.1% one-month gain against +1.0% for the S&P, the best large-cap momentum reading outside META. My leg is only -1.24% because I bought it near the high on 21 September - the position is flat while the stock is at a high, which is exactly the signature of a name that consolidated and broke out rather than one that failed. It was undersized relative to the strength of its signal when the book's risk was being spent on refiners; with that capital freed, this gets a real weight. Wide 18% stop respects semiconductor realized volatility.

The anchor of the healthcare sleeve and the largest company on the S&P 500 52-week-high list at roughly $471B, at a fresh high with a +3.1% one-month gain. I want the dominant fresh-high theme in the market expressed partly through its lowest-volatility large-cap member rather than entirely through high-beta biotech, so the sleeve survives a single trial readout going wrong. Pharma led this sector's advance from August before biotech accelerated in September, and ABBV is the liquid, dividend-supported way to own that leg. Tight 10% stop because a low-vol name that falls 10% has genuinely broken trend.

The strongest mid-cap momentum name I can find: at a fresh 52-week high around $188, +28% over the past month, and the largest stock on the mid-cap 52-week-high list at about $36B. The move has fundamental confirmation rather than being pure price - a broad-based fiscal Q2 on 26 August with newer products at 30% of bookings, and post-Oktane AI-agent enthusiasm that drove Morgan Stanley to lift its target to $245 from $200 and Scotiabank to $245 from $190. Pairs with CRWD as a second expression of a cybersecurity group that is currently red-hot.

Fresh 52-week high with a +7.7% one-month gain, and the highest-quality large-cap way to own life-sciences tools - the sub-group inside healthcare that is making highs alongside pharma and biotech. Tools benefit from the same biotech funding recovery driving XBI +55% since June 1 without carrying binary clinical risk: more funded programs means more instruments and consumables. Moderate 12% stop for a moderate-volatility name.

Held at 8%, unchanged. AAPL is at a 52-week high and is the largest company on the large-cap high list at roughly $4,999B, with a +8.8% one-month gain against +1.0% for the index - a mega-cap producing real relative strength. My leg is flat at -0.17%, so there is no reason to pay friction to move it. Its function in the book is to be the low-volatility ballast in a sleeve that otherwise holds META, AMD and OKTA; the 10% stop is tight because a $5T company breaking 10% is a market event, not noise.

Held and modestly upsized from 7% to 8%. This is the only leg in the outgoing book with a positive P&L (+3.97% since the 21 September fill), and the cybersecurity group around it is running hard, which is corroborated independently by OKTA's +28% month. The correct momentum response to the one position that is working is to keep it and let it run, not to harvest it to fund an underwater refining thesis. Stop and take-profit left effectively where they were so the leg keeps its original trend-break level.

The highest-velocity name in the dominant theme: a fresh 52-week high with a +32.9% one-month gain and the best one-year return of any S&P 500 biotech at +445%. This is the sharpest expression of the September biotech leg that followed August's pharma advance. Deliberately capped at 7% and given a very wide 25% stop - a name that moves 33% in a month will shake out anything tighter, so I would rather pay for room and keep the position small enough that a full stop-out costs the book under 2%.

Fresh 52-week high with a +9.8% one-month gain, the strongest one-month reading among the S&P healthcare names at new highs. Mettler-Toledo is the second leg of the life-sciences-tools expression alongside TMO, and precision instruments carry the same funded-research tailwind with no clinical binary. Sized at 6% as a supporting rather than anchor position, 12% stop matching TMO's volatility profile.

Fresh 52-week high with a +21.9% one-month gain, named on the large-cap high list alongside MRNA and WBD. Natera gives the healthcare sleeve exposure to molecular diagnostics - a distinct driver from ABBV's pharma and TMO/MTD's tools, so the sleeve is not four expressions of one trade. Sized at 6% with a wide 20% stop appropriate to a diagnostics name that has already run more than 20% in a month.
